items.title: GTA 6 has secret playlists, and all you have to do is scan a few posters to unlock them
items.summary: Kodak Black and The Vault nightclub each have their own unique playlist.
items.body: Rockstar's lengthy credits reveal just how massive the GTA 6 song list truly is, but you don't start the game with every radio station unlocked. Leonida has two secret playlists (both needed for 100% completion), and neither is particularly hard to unlock once you know where to look. The Sniper of La Perle , Kodak Black's 22-track playlist, becomes available as soon as you scan four posters around La Perle at TWA Ponya Tattoo, Drip Drops, Aunt Zola's Soul Food, and the Jack of Hearts nightclub. Then there's The Vault Radio , which only requires you to scan a single poster at the nightclub of the same name. The shops automatically marked themselves on my map as I drove around La Perle and Crosstown, but I've included screenshots highlighting their specific locations in Vice City's Haitian district. items.title: I didn't realize Etsy was selling bridges now
items.summary: The company says its new generative AI training agreement will only be used for good. Why would anyone believe that?
items.body: Online marketplace Etsy, best known as a platform for selling handmade goods, recently updated its user agreement to allow itself to "develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies" using content uploaded by sellers. This has not gone over well, with some closing their Etsy shops in protest. In response, Etsy has assured users that it doesn't plan to train AI systems designed to copy their work or replace their creativity. Instead, the company said that the change is about improving the platform and providing "services and tools that can help you run your business." I am sometimes sympathetic toward companies that get yelled at for normal terms of service agreements. If a company hosts user-submitted content on the web, for instance, it needs a license to distribute that content globally, and sometimes users misunderstand that. This is not one of those cases. items.body: If you want to move faster in Grand Theft Auto 6, I can't blame you: There's a lot I've enjoyed about the opening hours I've spent in Jason's shoes. He's handy with a nailgun. Which is fine! But there are plenty of times while roaming Leonida when you might wish he and Lucia were moving just a bit faster—just not so fast that you want to force them into a run. Luckily, Rockstar's got our back: There's a setting to bump up your basic movement speed without pushing a button. How to increase your movement speed in GTA 6 (Image credit: Rockstar) To change the pace that Jason and Lucia move at in GTA 6, head to Settings , move over to the Gameplay tab, and scroll down to the Movement section. items.body: تلقى بايرن ميونخ أنباء مقلقة خلال مواجهته أمام كولن، مساء الجمعة، ضمن منافسات الجولة العاشرة من الدوري الألماني. وجاء ذلك بعدما تعرض المهاجم الإنجليزي هاري كين لإصابة أجبرته على مغادرة أرض الملعب في وقت مبكر، بالتزامن مع معاناة زميله الفرنسي مايكل أوليسي من مشكلة بدنية استدعت تدخل الجهاز الطبي في الشوط الأول ثم استبداله في الاستراحة. وشهدت الدقيقة 15 من عمر المباراة تعرض كين لتدخل قوي من مدافع كولن جويل شميد داخل منطقة الجزاء، خلال محاولة المهاجم الإنجليزي الوصول إلى كرة عرضية، ليسقط على أرض الملعب متأثرًا بآلام في الكاحل، وسط قلق واضح من لاعبي الفريق البافاري. وحاول قائد المنتخب الإنجليزي استكمال اللقاء بعد تلقي الإسعافات الأولية، إلا أن شعوره بالألم حال دون استمراره، ليضطر المدرب البلجيكي فينسنت كومباني إلى إجراء تبديل اضطراري في الدقيقة 20، بإشراك توم بيشوف بدلًا منه. ولم تكن طريقة خروج كين مطمئنة بالنسبة للجهاز الفني لبايرن ميونخ، خصوصًا أن اللاعب اضطر إلى مغادرة الملعب بعد محاولته مواصلة اللعب، ما يفتح الباب أمام احتمالات غيابه عن المباريات المقبلة، انتظارًا لما ستكشف عنه الفحوصات الطبية بشأن طبيعة الإصابة ومدى خطورتها. وفي تطور آخر خلال الشوط الأول، احتاج الجناح الفرنسي مايكل أوليسي إلى تدخل الجهاز الطبي بعدما اشتكى من مشكلة بدنية، ما أثار المزيد من المخاوف داخل صفوف الفريق …

items.title: 21% of Rockstar staff have been employed by the company for over 10 years, which explains a lot about GTA 6's record-breaking launch
items.summary: It's easier to make successful games when you hold onto the people who know how.
items.body: If we're using Metacritic as a metric, Grand Theft Auto 6 is currently the best-reviewed game of all time . Between preorders and launch-day sales, it's already made over $3.7 billion in sales revenue. It's being lauded as a landmark achievement in game design, storytelling, and engineering. So how, exactly, did Rockstar pull it off? Well, the billion-dollar production budget certainly helped. But a Bloomberg report offers an important insight into how GTA 6 was able to deliver on its promises: According to a spokesperson, 21% of Rockstar's staff—roughly 1,000 people—have been employed by the company for over 10 years. For many of its development leads and directors, that figure is closer to 20 years, or higher. (Image credit: Rockstar) By retaining its employees for so long, Rockstar is able to capitalize on the kind of shared, institutional knowledge and honed creative process that developers build through years of collaboration. Now there's a rumour that the consumer Ryzen chip launch may have been pushed back to the second half of 2027. The new Ryzen offerings were originally thought to be launching in the first half, but Chiphell leaker Zhang Zhonghao says otherwise. In a post spotted by Videocardz , Zhang Zhonghao claims that the desktop chips, codenamed Olympic Ridge, have been switched to TSMC's N2X manufacturing process, and as a result the "timeline has been pushed back" (via machine translation). Zhang Zhonghao makes mention of Computex in their post, which some are speculating means a launch date after the show in June of next year. The issue appears to be fairly widespread going from reports on the Nvidia GeForce forum , Dell forum , Super User forum , and many, many threads on Reddit . Though that's a bunch of people that might, and did, notice random writes to their SSD; many more may not visit their task manager to check these things with any regularity. Except actually you can, as discovered by players on Reddit and tested by our own Morgan Park. It's easy enough to activate in-game. Go to the controller settings, then under the Controller Features section change your touch pad/select button to Camera 2 / 2. Get into a car, bring up your phone with the D-pad, press Circle or B then quickly hit Select. There you go, first-person GTA 6. As Morgan's footage shows, it's completely playable. It doesn't look 100% done, however, with your shoulders clipping through the camera when you've got a longarm gun up. While conspiracy theorists have convinced themselves that Rockstar is holding back this feature to sell it as DLC, I figure they're probably still polishing it to add in a future update. items.body: Six years into owning my PS5, I can count on one hand how many times the DualSense controller's resistive triggers have proved essential to the game I'm playing. They're key for Astro Bot's varied trigger-based mechanics, of course, and I wouldn't want to play Death Stranding 2 without my heavy backpack fighting back against me. But my new favorite use of the PS5 controller is GTA 6. GTA 6 uses the whole DualSense buffalo for a variety of sensory additives—I can feel it in the haptics when I roll over the rumble strip on the shoulders of roads or rear end another car—but the way it uses the triggers is especially effective. The resistive triggers activate when you'd expect, like while shooting guns, but they also come into play in activities that feel like they were designed around the controller: When swinging dumbbells, for instance, the triggers help me time when to release and start another rep. items.title: GTA 5's Steam concurrents have gone up rather than down now that GTA 6 is out, suggesting a lot of PC players are waiting
items.summary: We have GTA 6 at home.
items.body: Pour one out for the PC gamers who are now forced to watch everyone frolic in the streets of Grand Theft Auto 6 on consoles this week. The next best thing on PC is GTA 5, and its recent Steam concurrents suggest people are trying their best to fight the FOMO until Rockstar decides to bring the new one over. You might assume GTA 5 player counts would tank now that it's old news, but the numbers have actually jumped up a bit in the last month. SteamDB shows a peak of around 87,000 concurrent players in the last day, an almost 10% increase from October. There's been a bit of a dip today—which could partially be attributed to GTA 6 finally becoming available in every region—but it's not as sharp of a drop as you'd think it'd be for a 13-year-old game. In fact, GTA 5 has steadily kept a good amount of players over the last year, with major spikes happening around the occasional price discount. It usually hovers around 40,000 to 50,000 average concurrent players, and GTA 6's release hasn't broken the pattern. I'm of a mind with news writer Josh Wolens that the contrast between pre- and post-Endu gameplay really helps sell the game's power curve, but our coworkers Andy Chalk and Morgan Park both bounced off Queen's Domain's admittedly sluggish melee combat. items.summary: Ubisoft Montreal and Quebec are the latest to fall under the axe.
items.body: Ubisoft has laid off 166 people from its offices in Montreal and Quebec City, saying in a statement provided to PC Gamer that its "production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs." Founded in 1997, Ubisoft Montreal is one of the biggest game studios in the world, with roughly 4,000 employees as of 2022. Ubisoft Quebec, launched in 2005, is somewhat smaller but still substantial: Its website says the studio has "a team of over 600 creative, passionate, and innovative talents." The cuts reportedly impact employees who could not be assigned elsewhere after their existing projects were cancelled or rescoped. Whatever the reason, it's bleak: This is the latest round in a series of layoffs that have battered the company since it announced a major restructuring in January, which followed years of struggles including workplace misconduct scandals, persistent difficulties getting games launched , and underperformance among big releases. items.title: I just found a verrrry familiar-looking hat in GTA 6, and it was in the last place I would have expected
items.summary: Sometimes it pays to follow signs.
items.body: I just found a curious artifact of the Old West in GTA 6, and the best part is I stumbled across it completely by accident. That's right, partner: Arthur Morgan's cowboy hat is in Grand Theft Auto 6, and you won't find it in some trendy Western fashion shop or in a McMansion as part of a wealthy crypto bro's collection. If you want to wear it yourself, I'll tell you below where you can find it. How to find Arthur Morgan's cowboy hat (Image credit: Rockstar Games) I was out in Port Gellhorn looking for a particular kind of car for reasons completely unrelated to clothing accessories. While I was driving, I spotted a sign on the side of the road with a balloon tied to it, reading "Yard Sale" with an arrow pointing down the road. I followed the sign which led to more yard sale signs and, yup, sure enough, the signs pointed me to an actual yard sale. And among the items for sale was a very familiar-looking hat. It's called a "Genuine Cowboy Hat" and, this being a yard sale, it only cost $5. But I knew the second I saw it that this was no ordinary cowboy hat. Here, have a look at it from the back. In partnership with AimLabs, Corsair has made a mouse that can adjust sensitivity in different directions to tailor it to your movements and help you aim better. That's the claim, anyway. In practice, I've found that PureVector hasn't improved my aim, both subjectively while gaming and objectively based on multiple AimLabs tests. Some pro players that Corsair highlights claim it's helped them, so your mileage may vary. Apart from PureVector, though, the mouse itself deserves some attention, as it's still a very performant, lightweight mouse for competitive gaming. It has some upgrades compared to its predecessor, the Sabre V2 Pro , too. Buy if… ✅ You want to try the latest tech: You might get better results than I did with PureVector. It tailors sensor sensitivity in different directions based on how you aim. I've waited 13 years to play a new Grand Theft Auto game and the first thing I do when I finally get around to booting GTA 6 —and definitely not spoofing my home address to access it early—is jam a mouse and keyboard into my Xbox Series X just to see. GTA 5, once it made its way to PC, was always a game I played both with a keyboard and mouse and with a controller plugged in. Keeb and rodent for shooting, especially in the first-person mode, and the controller for just getting about in the game world. It was a real best of both worlds kinda thing that the PC does so well. It was the same with Red Dead Redemption 2, a game I completely avoided until it finally came to the PC. Keyboard and mouse for runnin' and gunnin' and a controller for horsin' around. Yeehaw.
